summary: Added an operator preflight guard for FeeAccumulator -> BuybackBurn FlushBuybackDue so premature flush attempts are blocked before caller-funded reserve can be donated to FeeAccumulator balance. The guard now also requires accepted M20F mainnet route-freeze evidence, so route_frozen alone is not enough for production reserve flush.
guarded_flow: FlushBuybackDue amount must equal the exact 51.05 TON funding envelope.
FeeAccumulator.buyback_due_ton must cover the exact envelope.
FeeAccumulator.buyback_burn_address must equal the intended BuybackBurn address.
M20F final mainnet route-freeze evidence must be accepted.
BuybackBurn fee_accumulator_address must equal the source FeeAccumulator address.

verification.focused_tests: npm.cmd run test:file -- tests\buyback-flush-preflight.test.ts tests\enable-buyback-split-preflight.test.ts tests\m20f-mainnet-route-freeze-preflight.test.ts tests\m20u-buybackburn-implementation-readiness.test.ts tests\buybackburn-production.test.ts tests\buybackburn-auth-negative-matrix.test.ts tests\fee-accumulator.test.ts tests\fee-accumulator-backing-negative.test.ts tests\m19h-buybackburn-funding-envelope.test.ts tests\m29-buybackburn-abi-freeze.test.ts

production_note: No contract bytecode changed. This is an operational guard for premature reserve flush and route-evidence mistakes; principal accounting in the FeeAccumulator -> BuybackBurn seam remains covered by existing contract tests.
